How it works: the watchdog runs as a foreground service. Whenever the open network with the SSID above is in range and the phone is not connected to it, the app re-joins it and keeps Wi-Fi alive even if Android thinks it has no internet. Right after connecting it sends the reboot command to the Starlink terminal over its local gRPC API (192.168.100.1:9200), the same call the official app makes. Grant location (needed by Android to scan Wi-Fi), keep Location turned on, and exclude the app from battery optimisation so it survives in the background.

%1$s is in range, but Android does not let the app manage it: the network is already saved in Wi-Fi settings by another owner. Forget it there (Open Wi-Fi settings) and the app will take over; until then the system auto-join is used.
